newsitem.title: UK: British Midland eyes European cargo hub.
newsitem.headline: British Midland eyes European cargo hub.

text.p: British Midland is considering establishing its own cargo hub operation on the continent, cargo manager Terry Greetham told Reuters.
The airline will start its first intra-Continental Europe service, between Cologne-Rome, on May 26,
"Due to open EU market conditions, we are now able to operate fifth freedom operations within Europe and I would like to see us develop a hub over there," he said.
He added that a location had yet to be determined, but mentioned Brussels and Cologne as important Western European express freight gateways.

From May 26, Cologne-Rome will be served as a once-daily extension to British Midland's twice-daily London Heathrow-Cologne service. It will be operated with Boeing 737-300 aircraft, which can uplift two to three tonnes of cargo per flight.
"Our market information says there should be good cargo business on the new route and we will soon be appointing a new cargo general sales agent in Germany to sell it," said Greetham.
--Bob Murphy, Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel +44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
